title: Serializer never skips hidden inputs despite the spec's own checked-off task claiming it does
detail: No `type === "hidden"` arm exists (grep confirms 'hidden' appears nowhere in form_draft.js). Any non-_-prefixed hidden input (a CSRF token field is the obvious candidate in this stack) serializes into the draft and round-trips on resume.
recommended_fix: Add `if (type === "hidden") return true;` to shouldSkipControl and pin it in form_draft.test.js, or correct the spec task if hidden-skip was dropped deliberately.

title: Migration header says erasure 'removes the row' while the same file's erased_at column keeps it as a tombstone
evidence:
+--   * Erasure — the continue email carries a self-service delete link
+--     (POST /apply/:code/draft-erasure/:token) that removes the row.

vs, lines later in the same file:
+  -- Erasure tombstone: a confirmed Art. 17 deletion wipes fields/token but
+  -- keeps the (vacancy, email) key until vacancy close so a still-open form
+  -- tab's next auto-save hits the upsert's erased_at guard instead of
+  -- silently re-creating the PII payload. Email kept as a suppression
+  -- record (GDPR-recognised) and disclosed on the erasure confirm page.
+  erased_at          TIMESTAMPTZ,
detail: Same-file contradiction: the header describes the pre-W3 hard-delete behaviour; the column comment describes the shipped tombstone. The migration header is a permanent record and is stale.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the header Erasure bullet to describe the tombstone (fields/token wiped, erased_at set, key retained until vacancy close).

title: Migration claims 'most rows have NULL (token minted lazily)' — this PR mints tokens at save time
evidence:
+-- continue_token is 288 bits of URL-safe entropy (wisp.random_string(48)),
+-- same capability model as application.erasure_token: the token IS the
+-- auth. Partial unique index — most rows have NULL (token minted lazily on
+-- the first "email me a link" request).

vs the spec change log in the same PR:
+  W1: tokens mint at SAVE time (upsert arg 4, COALESCE keeps existing) —
detail: With the W1 mint-at-save fix, every auto-saved draft gets a token on insert, so most rows will NOT have NULL and nothing is minted lazily. The index rationale comment misdescribes the shipped design.
recommended_fix: Update the comment: tokens minted at save via the upsert's COALESCE; the partial index enforces uniqueness over the minted majority.

title: Spec's Suggested Review Order still describes the expiry sweep as covering archived vacancies, contradicting its own W4 fix
evidence:
+- Expiry sweep phase: closed, archived, or past closes_at.
+  [`retention_job.gleam:314`](../../server/src/retention/retention_job.gleam#L314)

vs the same document's change log:
+  W4: archive no longer sweeps drafts (restorable; the emailed promise is
+  "until the vacancy closes").
detail: W4 reversed the earlier 'OR archived_at IS NOT NULL' sweep addition, but the review-order text still sends reviewers to a sweep described as 'closed, archived, or past closes_at'. Same-document contradiction.
recommended_fix: Change the review-order line to 'closed or past closes_at (archived deliberately kept — W4)'.

title: Continue-link response handling ignores HTTP status; save path was hardened to check res.ok in round 1
detail: Uniform-200 only covers send outcomes the handler controls. Any JSON-bodied non-200 (middleware 413, a JSON 500) lacking an explicit ok:false renders 'Link sent — check your inbox' for a rejected request.
recommended_fix: Mirror the save path: treat `!res || !res.ok` as CONTINUE_FAILED before trusting the body.

title: Continue-link flow has no closed-vacancy arm — saver stays enabled and copy promises a retry that can never succeed
detail: On a closed-vacancy continue-link response (ok:false, closed:true) the applicant sees 'Try again in a moment' — permanently false — and saverDisabled is never set, unlike the save path's terminal handling.
recommended_fix: Check body.closed in the continue-link handler: set saverDisabled and show closed-appropriate copy instead of the retry line.

title: Claimed copy sync with form_copy.gleam is enforced only by a comment; the 'copy pins' test never reads the Gleam source
evidence:
+  // Applicant-facing copy — KEEP IN SYNC with server/src/application/
+  // form_copy.gleam (same precedent as REVIEW_HINT_STEPPER in
+  // form_stepper.js: plain static JS can't import Gleam constants).

and the test:
+// ---------- Copy pins (sync with form_copy.gleam) ----------
+
+test("continue-link copy never blames the applicant and names no tech", () => {
+  assert.match(draft.CONTINUE_FAILED, /^Couldn\u2019t send/);
detail: The test regex-checks the JS constants against themselves; nothing compares them to form_copy.gleam. A Gleam-side copy edit drifts silently — the same class of gap round-1 N9 closed for event names via cross-require.
recommended_fix: Add a node test reading form_copy.gleam as text and asserting the shared strings appear verbatim, or drop the sync claim from both comments.

title: fakeTimers helper duplicated byte-identically across both new JS test files
detail: Identical ~20-line helper in both new test files violates the repo DRY rule (extract when logic repeats in 2+ places); a debounce-harness fix would need applying twice.
recommended_fix: Extract fakeTimers into a shared scripts/js-tests helper module and require it from both test files.

title: saveNow comment documents a `reason` parameter the function doesn't accept
evidence:
+    // saveNow(reason) → the debounced saver's inner call. Dedupes against
+    // the last acknowledged payload; failures leave state dirty so the next
+    // trigger (or the pagehide beacon) retries. Silent by design — the form
+    // itself never depends on the save succeeding.
+    function saveNow() {
detail: Leftover from a dropped logging/diagnostics argument; the documented signature and the actual signature disagree (same class of nit as round-1 N15).
recommended_fix: Drop '(reason)' from the comment, or add the parameter and use it.

evidence:
